ops.insert: 🤝 Wilson James — Meeting Prep (Chief of Staff)
30+ year UK company — security, aviation services, construction logistics
300+ clients — major airports, construction, events, facilities
Recently won JFK Airport (New Terminal One) — passenger assistance services in the US
Active at Birmingham Airport — one of their busiest contracts
CEO: Mark Dobson. Today's contact: Chief of Staff (second in command of entire business)
They have their own technology division — not just a security company, they invest in tech
2024 Annual Review: growing revenue, operating profits, expanding client base
THEIR PAIN POINTS — WHAT KEEPS THEM UP AT NIGHT
Managing welfare and safety concerns across 6,000 dispersed staff in high-pressure environments
Staff won't always report incidents through formal channels — fear of blame, culture, peer pressure
Insider threat is a rising problem in aviation — staff theft, misconduct, compliance breaches
Multi-site operations — no consistent real-time picture of what is happening across locations
SLA accountability — clients expect incident response times and audit trails
Scaling to US (JFK) means managing cultural, operational and compliance differences
Demonstrating duty of care to end clients (airports, facilities) — they need proof, not promises
"We've built a real-time safety intelligence platform that gives your teams on the ground a voice — and gives leadership an instant picture of what's happening, where, and how serious it is."
1. PEOPLE — Anonymous reporting via QR code means your staff speak up without fear. No app to download, no login, no trail back to them.
2. OPERATIONS — Live dashboard shows every incident, by severity, by zone, by time. Your operations team stops flying blind across multi-site.
3. PROOF — Full audit trail, SLA timers, AI-powered case management. You can show your clients exactly how you responded and when.

"The platform is built on Taskade Genesis — an enterprise AI workspace. That means every incident, case, and insight is stored, searchable, and can be turned into automated workflows. It's not just a reporting tool — it's a living intelligence system that gets smarter the more it's used."
Automations: when a critical incident is flagged, the right person is notified instantly — no manual chain of command needed
AI (ARIA): trained on all case data — can brief shift supervisors, suggest escalation actions, spot patterns before they become problems
Scales instantly — same system works for Birmingham Airport today and JFK tomorrow, no rebuild
LIKELY QUESTIONS + HOW TO ANSWER THEM
"What problem does this actually solve for us?"

"Right now, incidents happen that never get formally reported — staff don't feel safe speaking up, or the process is too slow. By the time leadership hears about something, it's already a problem. We change that. Your people can flag something in 30 seconds from any location, anonymously. You see it instantly. You act before it escalates."
"How is this different from what we already have?"

"Most systems are built for after the fact — logging what happened. This is built for right now. The live map, the AI triage, the SLA countdown — it's a command centre, not a spreadsheet. And because it's built on an AI platform, it learns and improves with your data."
"Can this work at scale — across airports, multiple sites?"

"Yes — by design. You can have one platform covering Birmingham, JFK, and every other site simultaneously. Each site has its own zones, its own QR codes, its own reporting — but leadership sees everything in one place. No additional installs, no extra licences per site."
"What does implementation look like? How long?"

"We can have a pilot site live within days — not months. There's no software to install for users, just QR codes placed in locations. The management dashboard is web-based. We configure your zones, your categories, your escalation rules — then it's live. We can start with one site and prove value before rolling out."

"We price this based on scale and configuration. For an organisation of your size across multiple sites, we'd put together a tailored proposal. What I'd suggest today is agreeing to run a pilot — let the numbers speak first." [Do NOT commit to a price in the room — ask to follow up]

"We've built this specifically for the security and facilities management space. Wilson James would be our flagship enterprise partner — which also means you shape how it evolves. We're not selling you an off-the-shelf box, we're building alongside you."
"Is this GDPR compliant? Where does the data go?"

"The platform is anonymous by design — we collect zero personal data from reporters. No name, no email, nothing that identifies the individual. Because there's no personal data, the GDPR exposure is minimal. Infrastructure is enterprise-grade, encrypted end-to-end, and we can provide full data processing documentation on request."
"How are your teams currently reporting welfare or safety concerns on site today?"
"When an incident happens at one of your sites, how quickly does leadership typically know about it?"
"With JFK coming online — how are you thinking about keeping operational visibility consistent across UK and US?"
"Are your clients — the airports — asking you for better reporting or incident data as part of their contracts?"
"What would success look like for you in the first 90 days of something like this?"
"Who else internally would need to be involved in a decision like this?" [Identify the real decision maker]
DEMO FLOW — WHAT TO SHOW & IN WHAT ORDER
Open the live map — show zones, real-time incident pins, severity colour coding. Say: "This is what your operations team sees right now."
Show the QR code on your phone — scan it, fill in a concern in 20 seconds. Watch it appear live on the map. Say: "This is what your staff see — no app, no login, 30 seconds."
Show the critical alert notification appearing — say: "The right person gets notified instantly. No waiting for shift handover."
Show ARIA — ask it a question about the incident. Say: "This is your AI safety lead. It knows every case, suggests actions, and can brief anyone in seconds."
Show the analytics / stats panel — 6 total, 1 critical, 2 high. SLA timer. Say: "This is what you show your client when they ask 'how did you handle it?'"
Do NOT try to close a sale in this meeting — the goal is to agree a pilot
Suggested close: "What I'd love to do is pick one site — Birmingham or wherever makes sense — and run this for 30 days. No big commitment. Let the data tell the story."
Ask for a follow-up: "Who else should be part of the next conversation — operations, HR, IT?"
Send follow-up within 2 hours: brief summary, what was shown, proposed next step, security/GDPR doc
KEY THINGS TO REMEMBER IN THE ROOM
The Chief of Staff thinks strategically — connect everything back to scale, risk, and reputation
They are expanding internationally — position this as infrastructure for that growth, not just a reporting tool
Their end clients (airports) hold them accountable — help them see this makes THEM look better to their clients
Don't oversell the tech — let the demo do the work. Keep your language simple and outcome-focused
If they ask something you don't know: "Great question — I'll confirm that in writing after the meeting"
Be confident — you have a working, live product. Very few people walk in with that.
